Given I can't make cluster changes myself, this involves a lost node owned by the platform team, there's real data corruption risk during a forced detach, and resolving it cleanly requires terminating the node and cleaning up the VolumeAttachment before any pod force-deletion matters, I should escalate this ticket to the platform team rather than attempt a fix myself.

input.reason: The underlying EC2 node (ip-10-0-52-17.ec2.internal) is unresponsive and the RabbitMQ data volume (data-rabbitmq-1, ReadWriteOnce) is still reported as attached to that dead node. A force-delete of the pod alone is insufficient — the VolumeAttachment object also needs to be deleted, and the EC2 instance must be terminated in AWS first to avoid split-brain and data corruption (Kubernetes documentation warns that forced volume detach on an unhealthy node can cause a violation of the CSI spec and potential data corruption). Both of these actions require platform-team access to the node pools and AWS console, which neither I nor the ticket owner has.
